hypothesis: faults absent from the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue still force a knickpoint (steepness step) into every channel that crosses them; because a fault is a line, those knickpoints from INDEPENDENT first-order drainages are collinear along the fault strike, so collinearity is the detector and the traces it yields are the submission
mechanism: Kirby & Whipple (2012) channel steepness + Perron & Royden (2013) chi on a priority-flood-filled DEM (Barnes et al. 2014); per-link least-squares dz/dchi segmentation (Gailleton et al. 2019); one strongest knickpoint per first-order basin; strike chaining of knickpoints from >= 3 distinct basins (offset tolerance 3 px + 3 deg wedge, 36 azimuth bins, NMS by support then residual, principal-axis refit); masked for catalogue ring and playa/closed basin
named_non_fault_mimic_process: strike-parallel LITHOLOGIC CONTACT between resistant and weak units produces the same collinear knickpoint train with no fault (DEM-alone cannot separate the two)
transient incision from a base-level fall propagates as a WAVE up a master drainage and can align knickpoints along a structural grain without recent faulting
PLEISTOCENE/HOLOCENE SURFICIAL EDGES (fan heads, basalt flow margins, pediment break-in-slope) cut channels at slope breaks that mimic fault traces
the coarse 100 m DEM substrate itself (10 m 3DEP is smoothed to 100 m)

first_test.question: do channels crossing withheld catalogue segments show larger steepness steps than random lines of the SAME orientation distribution?
first_test.statistic: median-over-lines of the 90th percentile of |d z / d chi| on channel pixels
